title: Ezekiel Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who came unto Ezekiel and sat before him at the beginning of Ezekiel Chapter 14?
options: Certain of the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Certain of the elders of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:1 states that certain of the elders of Israel came unto Ezekiel and sat before him.

questions.question: What came unto Ezekiel after the elders sat before him?
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:2 clearly says, 'And the word of the LORD came unto me.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:3, what have the men set up in their heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:3 states that these men have set up their idols in their heart.

questions.question: What does God say He will do when a man of Israel sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet?
options: Answer him according to the multitude of his idols
questions.correctAnswer: Answer him according to the multitude of his idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:4 states that God will answer him that comes according to the multitude of his idols.

questions.question: Why does the LORD say He will take the house of Israel in their own heart?
options: Because they are estranged from Him through their idols
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are estranged from Him through their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:5 explains that the house of Israel is estranged from the LORD through their idols.

questions.question: What does the LORD command the house of Israel to do concerning their idols?
options: Repent and turn away from their idols
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and turn away from their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:6 instructs the house of Israel to repent and turn themselves from their idols and abominations.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will answer those who set up idols in their hearts through a prophet by Himself.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:7 states that God will answer such a man by Himself.

questions.question: What will the LORD do to the man who sets up idols in his heart and comes to a prophet?
options: Set His face against him and make him a sign and a proverb
questions.correctAnswer: Set His face against him and make him a sign and a proverb
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:8 says God will set His face against that man, make him a sign and a proverb, and cut him off from among His people.

questions.question: True or False: If a prophet is deceived when he speaks, the LORD says He Himself has deceived that prophet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:9 states that if a prophet is deceived, the LORD has deceived him and will destroy him.

questions.question: What punishment will the prophet and the one who seeks him bear according to Ezekiel 14?
options: Both will bear the punishment of their iniquity
Only the prophet will be punished
Only the seeker will be punished
questions.correctAnswer: Both will bear the punishment of their iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:10 states that the punishment of the prophet shall be as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him.

questions.question: True or False: The purpose of the LORD's punishments is so Israel will no longer go astray or be polluted with transgressions.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:11 explains that the punishments are so Israel may become the LORD's people and He their God.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 14, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Repent and turn from your idols
Set up idols in your heart
Come to a prophet to enquire
questions.correctAnswer: Set up idols in your heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:3-4 indicate that the initial act is setting up idols in the heart, before any other actions or consequences occur.

questions.question: Who are the three men mentioned as examples of righteousness in Ezekiel 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, Daniel, and Job
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 explicitly names Noah, Daniel, and Job as righteous men.

questions.question: True or False: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in the land during its punishment, they could save their children as well.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:16 states they would deliver only their own souls, not their sons or daughters.

questions.question: What four sore judgments does the LORD mention as coming upon Jerusalem?
options: Sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence
questions.correctAnswer: Sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21 lists these four judgments upon Jerusalem.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:9, what happens if a prophet is deceived when he speaks?
options: The LORD has deceived the prophet and will destroy him from among His people
The prophet will be forgiven if he repents
The prophet's words will bring blessings to Israel
The prophet will be promoted among the elders
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has deceived the prophet and will destroy him from among His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:9 states that if the prophet is deceived when he speaks, it is because the LORD has deceived him, and He will stretch out His hand to destroy him from the midst of Israel. This shows God's judgment on false prophecy.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 14:10 say both the prophet and the one who seeks him will bear?
options: The punishment of their iniquity equally
Only the prophet will be punished
Only the seeker will be punished
questions.correctAnswer: The punishment of their iniquity equally
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:10 explains that the punishment of the prophet will be the same as that of the one who seeks him, indicating shared responsibility for iniquity.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 14:11 describe God's purpose in punishing Israel to prevent them from going astray?
options: That Israel may be His people and He may be their God
That Israel may be destroyed completely
That Israel may be scattered among the nations
That Israel may build new idols
questions.correctAnswer: That Israel may be His people and He may be their God
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:11 states God's aim is that Israel no longer goes astray or is polluted by transgressions, but becomes His people and He their God, emphasizing restoration and faithfulness.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:13, what will God do when the land sins grievously against Him?
options: Break the staff of bread and send famine, cutting off man and beast
Build a city for the people
questions.correctAnswer: Break the staff of bread and send famine, cutting off man and beast
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:13 explains that grievous sin will cause God to stretch out His hand, break the staff of bread (symbolizing sustenance), send famine, and cut off both man and beast from the land.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 14:14 say about the righteousness of Noah, Daniel, and Job if they were in a sinful land?
options: They would only deliver their own souls by their righteousness
They would save the entire land
They would be ignored by God
They would become leaders of the land
questions.correctAnswer: They would only deliver their own souls by their righteousness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 emphasizes that even the righteousness of Noah, Daniel, and Job would only save themselves, not others, illustrating the severity of the land's sin and judgment.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 14:16 describe if noisome beasts spoil the land?
options: Neither sons nor daughters will be delivered, only the righteous individuals
The entire family will be saved
The beasts will be driven away by the people
The land will become fertile again
questions.correctAnswer: Neither sons nor daughters will be delivered, only the righteous individuals
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:16 states that even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were present, only they would be saved, not their descendants, showing the extent of desolation caused by the beasts.

questions.question: Based on Ezekiel 14:17-18, what happens if God sends a sword through the land?
options: Only the righteous will be delivered, not their sons or daughters
The sword will miss the righteous
The whole family of the righteous will be spared
The sword will only kill animals
questions.correctAnswer: Only the righteous will be delivered, not their sons or daughters
questions.explanation: Verses 17 and 18 explain that when God sends a sword to cut off man and beast, even the righteous will only save themselves, not their children, emphasizing individual responsibility and judgment.

questions.question: Ezekiel 14:19-20 says that if God sends a pestilence, who will be delivered?
options: Only Noah, Daniel, and Job will deliver their own souls
Everyone in the land will be saved
Only the children of the righteous will be saved
questions.correctAnswer: Only Noah, Daniel, and Job will deliver their own souls
questions.explanation: These verses reiterate that even during a pestilence, only the righteous individuals themselves will be saved, not their families or the land, highlighting personal righteousness.

questions.question: What four sore judgments does Ezekiel 14:21 list that God will send upon Jerusalem?
options: Sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence
questions.correctAnswer: Sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21 clearly lists the four judgments: sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence, as God's method to cut off man and beast from Jerusalem.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:22, what will remain in Jerusalem after the judgments?
options: A remnant of sons and daughters who will be brought forth
No one will be left alive
questions.correctAnswer: A remnant of sons and daughters who will be brought forth
questions.explanation: Verse 22 promises that despite the severity of judgments, a remnant of sons and daughters will be preserved, offering hope and restoration.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 14:23 say the remnant will comfort the people?
options: By their ways and doings showing that God's actions were just
By bringing offerings to the LORD
By sending messages to the nations
questions.correctAnswer: By their ways and doings showing that God's actions were just
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states the remnant will comfort the people through their righteous living, proving that God's judgments were justified.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 14:11 teaches that God's punishment is meant to cause Israel to never stray again and to be His people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:11 explicitly states that the punishment is intended so Israel may no longer stray or be polluted but be God's people, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 14:14 says that having righteous individuals like Noah, Daniel, and Job in a sinful land will save the entire population.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 clarifies that even these righteous men would only save themselves, not the whole land, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 14:10 teaches that the punishment for the prophet is different from the punishment for the person who seeks him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:10 states that the punishment of the prophet is the same as the punishment of the one who seeks him, so they share equal responsibility, making the statement false.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience and trust in God can be drawn from Ezekiel 14:9-11 regarding false prophecy?
options: Trust only in God's word and avoid seeking guidance from false prophets
Ignore the word of God and seek worldly advice
Rely on multiple prophets to confirm a message
questions.correctAnswer: Trust only in God's word and avoid seeking guidance from false prophets
questions.explanation: Verses 9-11 warn that false prophecy leads to destruction for both prophet and seeker, emphasizing the need to trust God's true word and repent, not idols or false guidance.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14, what will happen to the sons and daughters even if righteous men like Noah, Daniel, and Job are in the land during a sword judgment?
options: They will be saved along with the righteous men
They will be delivered but the land will be desolate
They will not be delivered, only the righteous men themselves
They will be protected from the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will not be delivered, only the righteous men themselves
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:18 states that though these three men were in the land, they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters; they only shall be delivered themselves, indicating the judgment spares only the righteous individuals.

questions.question: What are the four sore judgments that the Lord GOD declares He will send upon Jerusalem in Ezekiel 14?
questions.correctAnswer: Sword, famine, noisome beast, pestilence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21 lists the four sore judgments as the sword, famine, noisome beast, and pestilence sent to cut off man and beast from Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 14, what does the Lord say will be the purpose of leaving a remnant in Jerusalem after the judgments?
options: To be a sign of hope for other nations
To come forth, show their ways and doings, and provide comfort
questions.correctAnswer: To come forth, show their ways and doings, and provide comfort
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:22 explains that a remnant will be left, who shall come forth and their way and doings will be seen, comforting the people regarding the evil brought upon Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which Old Testament figures are mentioned in Ezekiel 14 as examples of righteousness who could only save themselves in times of judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, Daniel, Job
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14, 20 mention Noah, Daniel, and Job as the righteous men whose righteousness could only deliver their own souls during the land's judgment.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'stumblingblock' in Ezekiel 14:3 signify in the context of Israel's sin?
options: An obstacle causing sin or error
questions.correctAnswer: An obstacle causing sin or error
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'stumblingblock' (michshol) in Ezekiel 14:3 refers to an obstacle or cause of sin, symbolizing how idols in the heart cause Israel to err and fall into iniquity.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 14:14–20 when describing judgments and the fate of righteous men and their families?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14–20 uses parallelism by repeating similar phrases about judgments (sword, pestilence, noisome beasts) and the fate of Noah, Daniel, and Job to emphasize the certainty and severity of God's judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:9, what consequence does the prophet face if he is deceived when speaking a thing from the LORD?
options: He will be forgiven if he repents
He will be destroyed from the midst of the people
He will be punished with exile
questions.correctAnswer: He will be destroyed from the midst of the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:9 declares that if the prophet is deceived, the LORD Himself has deceived him and will stretch out His hand to destroy that prophet from among the people of Israel.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of a remnant being preserved after judgment, similar to Ezekiel 14:22-23?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 10:20-22
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:20-22 speaks of a remnant of Israel returning to the LORD after judgment, echoing the theme in Ezekiel 14:22-23 where a remnant is left to provide comfort and testify to God's justice.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 14:13, what is the 'staff of the bread' that the LORD says He will break as part of His judgment on the land?
options: The agricultural productivity and food supply
questions.correctAnswer: The agricultural productivity and food supply
questions.explanation: The 'staff of the bread' in Ezekiel 14:13 symbolizes the land's provision of food, so breaking it refers to causing famine by cutting off the sustenance for man and beast.

questions.question: What is the significance of the LORD answering those who seek Him 'according to the multitude of his idols' as stated in Ezekiel 14:4?
options: God will give multiple answers to confuse them
God's response will be influenced by their idolatry, reflecting their unfaithfulness
God rewards their persistence despite idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: God's response will be influenced by their idolatry, reflecting their unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:4 explains that the LORD will answer according to the multitude of idols set up in their hearts, indicating that their idolatry affects the nature of His response, showing His judgment.

questions.question: Ezekiel 14:7-8 states that the LORD will set His face against a man who sets up idols in his heart and seeks a prophet. What will be the result for that man?
options: He will be blessed for his faith
He will be made a sign and proverb and cut off from among the people
He will be given a chance to repent without punishment
He will become a prophet himself
questions.correctAnswer: He will be made a sign and proverb and cut off from among the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:8 states that God will set His face against such a man, making him a sign and proverb and cutting him off from the midst of His people.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 14 teaches that repentance from idols is necessary for Israel to be restored as God's people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:6 calls the house of Israel to repent and turn from their idols so that they may no longer be polluted and may be God's people, showing repentance is necessary.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God's judgment coming upon a rebellious people as in Ezekiel 14's four sore judgments?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 6:7-8
questions.explanation: Revelation 6:7-8 describes the coming of the fourth horseman bringing death by sword, famine, and pestilence, paralleling Ezekiel 14:21's four sore judgments.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 14:10 say about the relationship between the punishment of the prophet and the person who seeks him?
options: The prophet will be punished more harshly
The person seeking will be punished but the prophet spared
They will both bear the same punishment
questions.correctAnswer: They will both bear the same punishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:10 states that the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him, showing they share consequences.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 14 shows that even the most righteous individuals can fully deliver their families from divine judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14-20 demonstrates that even righteous men like Noah, Daniel, and Job can only deliver their own souls, not their sons or daughters, from judgment.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:3, what have the elders of Israel set up in their hearts?
questions.correctAnswer: Idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:3 states that the elders have set up their idols in their heart, indicating internal idolatry.

questions.question: What is the Lord's response toward a man who comes to a prophet with idols in his heart according to Ezekiel 14:4?
options: He answers according to the multitude of his idols
He sends an angel to guide him
questions.correctAnswer: He answers according to the multitude of his idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:4 explains that God will answer a man according to the multitude of his idols, reflecting God's judgment on idolatry.

questions.question: What reason does God give in Ezekiel 14:5 for taking the house of Israel in their own heart?
options: Because they are estranged from Him through their idols
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are estranged from Him through their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:5 states that God takes Israel in their own heart because they are estranged from Him through their idols.

questions.question: Which doctrine is emphasized in Ezekiel 14:6 regarding the people's required response to idolatry?
options: Repentance and turning away from idols
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance and turning away from idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:6 calls for repentance and turning away from idols, highlighting the doctrine of sanctification and repentance.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 14:8 reveal about God's attribute when He sets His face against a man who sins with idols in his heart?
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:8 shows God's holiness and justice by setting His face against those who persist in idolatry and punishing them accordingly.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 14:9 describe for a prophet who is deceived in his prophecy?
options: God will stretch out His hand and destroy him from among His people
He will be forgiven without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God will stretch out His hand and destroy him from among His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:9 teaches that if a prophet is deceived, God Himself will act to destroy that prophet, demonstrating God's righteous judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 14:11 describe God's purpose in punishing Israel and their prophets?
options: To prevent Israel from going astray and to purify them as His people
To show favoritism to other nations
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent Israel from going astray and to purify them as His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:11 states God punishes to keep Israel from straying and to purify them into His people, highlighting God's sanctifying purpose.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 14:14, which three men are mentioned as models of righteousness who could only save their own souls if the land sinned grievously?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, Daniel, and Job
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 names Noah, Daniel, and Job as righteous men whose righteousness could only save themselves, emphasizing individual responsibility.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 14:19-20 teach about God's judgment through pestilence on the land?
options: Even the righteous can only save their own souls, not their families
The entire land will be spared
questions.correctAnswer: Even the righteous can only save their own souls, not their families
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:19-20 explains that during pestilence, even righteous men like Noah, Daniel, and Job can only save themselves, underscoring God's sovereign judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 14:22, what will remain in Jerusalem after God's four sore judgments?
options: A remnant of sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: A remnant of sons and daughters
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:22 promises that a remnant will be left after judgments, emphasizing the doctrine of God's preservation of a faithful remnant.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 14:5 and Ezekiel 14:6 together inform the doctrine of human responsibility and divine judgment?
options: Idolatry estranges humans from God, requiring repentance to avoid judgment
Humans are not responsible for idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: Idolatry estranges humans from God, requiring repentance to avoid judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:5 shows estrangement through idols, and 14:6 calls for repentance, highlighting human responsibility to turn from sin to avoid God's judgment.

questions.question: What theological insight do Ezekiel 14:8 and Ezekiel 14:9 provide about God's justice and the role of prophets?
options: God holds both sinners and prophets accountable, enforcing justice impartially
Prophets are always exempt from judgment
God punishes only the people, not the prophets
God does not intervene in prophetic errors
questions.correctAnswer: God holds both sinners and prophets accountable, enforcing justice impartially
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:8 punishes the sinner, while 14:9 punishes the deceived prophet, showing God's impartial justice on all parties.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s judgments are unjust because even the righteous suffer along with the wicked. What does Ezekiel 14:14-20 teach about this?
options: Righteousness only saves the individual’s soul, but corporate judgment affects the land and people
God punishes the righteous and wicked equally without cause
The righteous protect their families from judgment
Judgment is random and unrelated to righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness only saves the individual’s soul, but corporate judgment affects the land and people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:14-20 explains that even righteous men can only save themselves during corporate judgment, showing God’s justice in punishing communal sin but preserving individual salvation.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 14:21-23 contribute to the narrative arc of redemption concerning judgment and restoration?
options: God’s judgments are severe but He preserves a remnant for future comfort and restoration
Judgment is final with no hope for restoration
Restoration is based on human effort alone
God abandons His people after judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgments are severe but He preserves a remnant for future comfort and restoration
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:21-23 concludes with God preserving a remnant after judgment, pointing to redemptive hope and restoration in His covenant plan.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 14:7 reveal about God’s attribute concerning His personal involvement with those who seek Him despite idolatry?
questions.correctAnswer: God Himself will answer them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 14:7 states that God will answer by Himself those who come to prophets with idols in their hearts, showing His personal sovereignty and authority.
